description: Alaska Ocean Observing System | An IOOS Regional Data Portal is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Integrated Ocean Observing System | Federal Partners; Integrated Ocean Observing System | Regional Associations; Alliance for Coastal Technologies (ACT). As the “eye on Alaska’s coasts and oceans,” Alaska Ocean Observing System (AOOS) represents a network of critical ocean and coastal observations. Data available through the site describe the status of Alaska’s marine ecosystem and can inform decisions about use of the marine environment. Coverage: Alaska and its surrounding waters. The toolkit lists hazards: Changing Seasons, Erosion and Shoreline Recession, Flooding – General, Shifting Species, Habitats, and Ecosystems. Assets: Aquatic and Marine Resources, Natural Areas and Wildlife, Property, Water Infrastructure – Stormwater. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
